posts.text:
One vendor is cheaper on the cheese. Then delivery flips the bill.

The other vendor raised the price last week.

I’m building Never86’d for the operator who has to chase both answers. Here’s the updated sample.

Watch each vendor against last week. Compare the product, case weight and amount you need.

Then check delivery, stock and the order minimum.

A lower case price can still mean a bigger order.

In our fictional example: $6 less on cheese becomes $6 more with delivery.

Change one detail. The explanation changes.

Draft the vendor question, name an owner and ask for the reply. No message is sent in this sample.

The goal: one useful answer and a clear next move in ten minutes. Real operator sessions still need to prove it.

Live AI, photo reading and accounts are still being built. Planned offer: one location, one free seat. Extra manager seats paid.

Try the updated sample: https://never86-bnt24t594-myke-muellers-projects.vercel.app/demo/operator

Made up records. Working calculations.

What would change your next order?

Myke, founder of Never86’d.
